narration: If you're hearing this, Ward pulled the file like I asked her to. At three-oh-three I let it take me. Walking felt like being carried. The field didn't open like a door — it opened like an eye. Light under the grass, drawn in perfect lines, warm as a heartbeat. I remember looking up. I remember being counted. They found the field empty at dawn. Forty-one of us walked in. The official report says we all walked home. Check your ceiling tonight. If you hear the hum — don't count the beats.

shots.prompt: Detective Aras Kaya (t-shirt, dog tags of a badge on the lanyard) straps a small chest-mounted bodycam to himself at his desk, presses record so its tiny light blinks, then pins a handwritten note and his badge to the center of the evidence board. Ends on: the blinking bodycam light in the lamplit office.

3 AM: Detective Aras Kaya, barefoot in a t-shirt, walks the centerline of the suburban street with eyes closed, face slack, the tiny bodycam light blinking on his chest — falling into step among other sleepwalkers in nightclothes under the sodium lights. Ends on: Aras absorbed into the walking line.

The sleepwalkers file into the moonlit field and assemble into their vast grid; camera drifts slowly through the rows of still figures and closes on Detective Aras Kaya standing among them, eyes closed, breath fogging, bodycam light blinking. Ends on: close on Aras's sleeping face.

Under the standing crowd, thin seams of pale light ignite in the grass — a perfect luminous lattice spreading across the whole field between the rows of sleepwalkers, mist glowing, and every head tilts up toward the sky in one motion. Ends on: the glowing lattice field of upturned faces.

The lattice light swells until the standing figures become silhouettes inside brightness — then cuts to black silence, and a beat later: the field at dawn, completely empty, a vast geometric lattice of flattened, scorched grass where the crowd stood. Ends on: the burned lattice pattern under the sunrise.

Morning light through the blinds: Dr. Lena Ward (lab coat folded over her arm) stands at Aras's desk before the evidence board, holding his recovered muddy bodycam. On the desk monitor, static resolves into a single slow synchronized waveform crawling across the screen. She looks up from it. Ends on: the waveform pulsing on the monitor beside his pinned badge.
